messages:
sophia: Heads up — we're seeing a weird pattern of GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 starting ~09:10 UTC. Small inference jobs get scheduled, run a few mins, then get preempted with no obvious capacity shortage. Logs show repeated prebind/reschedule churn.

oliver: Seen it too, looks like a stair-step of evictions across AZs. esp ap-southeast1-b. Any recent scheduler config changes? :thinking_face:

maya: Not that I'm aware of. I grabbed the node taint history — several nodes got a taint added by the node-health controller around 09:08 but then removed quickly. Could be oscillation.

sophia: paste of pod event for one of the failed pods:```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age    From               Message
  ----    ------     ----   ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  5m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ...
  Warning Preempted  3m     kube-scheduler      preempted by higher priority pod
  Normal  Scheduled  2m     default-scheduler  Re-scheduled on different node
  Warning Preempted  30s    kube-scheduler      preempted again
```

prateek: That preempted message is the important bit. Could be fractional GPU spread + affinity causing the scheduler to prefer packing that then gets evicted when a larger gang joins. Any recent burst of large training jobs?

karla: We had a big Dedicated batch kickoff ~09:00 (reserved pool autoscale). It might be stealing slots. But rate of small-pod churn is higher than I'd expect for that.

oliver: Quick check: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending` shows a lot of pending tiny-gpu pods with nodeAffinity for nvlink label. Looks like affinity+taint interplay.

maya: Also seeing chain of node drains from the thermal monitor on a subset of racks — they add a taint `hardware/tempering=true:NoSchedule` then remove. If the scheduler sees temporary capacity holes it may reassign pods, then when taints are removed large batch jobs reflow and evict smaller ones.

sophia: Proposed mitigations: 1) increase preemption buffer for small pods (lower priority for big jobs) 2) temporarily disable canary cluster rollback we rolled last week 3) enable `PreferNoSchedule` for thermal taint instead of hard NoSchedule to reduce churn. Thoughts?

prateek: (1) is quick but might violate SLA for Dedicated. If we lower priority for batch, we should do it only for non-dedicated labels.

karla: (3) seems safe to try in ap-southeast1-c first. Switching taint effect to PreferNoSchedule will still try to avoid nodes but won't force reschedules when taint toggles.

oliver: I can patch node-health-controller to flip the taint effect to PreferNoSchedule for the thermal taint in ap-southeast1-c and monitor for 30m. Rolling change, one AZ at a time.

infra-bot: deploy started by oliver:PATCH node-health-controller (ap-southeast1-c) — rollout id r-4521. Check /incidents for live metrics.

maya: After the patch we should watch `scheduler_preemption_count` and `pod_eviction_total` and tokenized GPU packing histograms. I'm seeing preemption_count spike ~09:12 to 240/min earlier.

sophia: Also consider adding a short prefix/KV cache pin for small pods so they tolerate transient reschedules — reduces cold-start cost and pressure. Longer-term: scheduler should be more aware of reserved pools vs burst pools.

prateek: Agreed. For quick rollback plan: if evictions don't drop within 20m in the AZ we revert the patch. oliver, can you also tag the nodes with `redwood/experiment=thermal-prefer-nosched` so metrics filter works?

oliver: Yep tagging now. Patch applied to ap-southeast1-c. Watching.

karla: Noted a small improvement — preemption_count down ~40% in c but b still noisy. Can we stagger b next?

sophia: Stagger b after 10m if stable. Also notify sales/customer-success for potential transient perf hits in ap-southeast1 customers.

oliver: Starting ap-southeast1-b patch now. infra-bot:deploy r-4522.

infra-bot: deploy succeeded (r-4522) — all node-health-controller instances updated in ap-southeast1-b.

maya: Early signal: evictions in b down ~55% and pending tiny pods drain faster. Looks promising.

prateek: Good call. Follow-ups: 1) add a scheduler experiment to respect `redwood/reserved-pool` label to avoid evicting small inference pods from reserved capacity 2) longer-term we need packing heuristics that avoid oscillating decisions when taints are flapping.

sophia: I'll create an RFC for scheduler heuristics and reserved-pool affinity. For now, leave the PreferNoSchedule change in place and run for 24h across ap-southeast1. If anything unexpected, revert.

karla: I'll notify ops and add a page to the runbook about thermal-taint behavior and this mitigation. :white_check_mark:

oliver: Leaving monitoring on. Ping me if evictions creep back up.

sophia: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the RFC and a short retro mañana. :coffee:
